correctness.rationale: For iid uniform two-sphere points, one pair has F_Z(z)=z²/(1+z²) and E Z=E(1/Z)=π/2. Distinct edge ratios are pairwise independent by conditional rotation invariance. Their simultaneous large-event probabilities are O(x^-4), which supplies a complete finite-N one-big-pair proof of the two-ray vague measure with coefficient N(2/n)²=2(n-1)/n. Scalar tail constants, exact moment threshold p=2, log-truncated second-moment coefficient, and upper-quantile inversion follow by integration. The explicit checker independently corroborated 64 numerical conditions; none is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The published two-sphere test is almost surely computable but of infinite variance. Exact one-sided null-tail coefficients and its two-ray parameter dependence supply a motivated extreme-level p-value approximation and explain how near-collision versus near-antipodal pairs drive false rejections. The log-truncated-moment coefficient quantifies sensitivity of variance-based approximations to cutoff. All are natural invariants of the source statistic, with an explicit need for extreme-level calibration, not a merely renamed known infinite-variance observation.
